summary: Mr. Arking reviews historical community customs regarding eating dried legumes, fresh legumes, and rice on Pesah in Halab and other Middle Eastern and North African communities. He outlines the reasons behind these practices and how they evolved over time due to historical circumstances like food shortages. He also explains how these traditions were preserved or modified in Jerusalem, Morocco, Baghdad, Tunisia, Djerba, and modern New York.
